edits.find:
Murmur Man puts you on a body part and breathing picks the tenant. Decrescendo diastolic is the right arm — the tail falling away from S2 — and that arm holds exactly two valves, aortic and pulmonic regurgitation. Six options collapse to two. Then increases with inspiration means right heart: pulmonic regurgitation.

Everything else corroborates. Single S2 means a component is gone, here P2, because the pulmonic valve is incompetent. The parasternal heave is the dilated right ventricle carrying the volume load. And the etiology is in the history: repairing tetralogy of Fallot requires enlarging the outflow tract, which disrupts the pulmonic annulus.

Single S2 means one component is gone; here P2 is lost because the pulmonic valve is incompetent. The parasternal heave is the dilated right ventricle carrying the volume load. Repair of tetralogy of Fallot is the etiology, because it requires enlarging the outflow tract, which disrupts the pulmonic annulus.

edits.find:
A holosystolic murmur at the left lower sternal border in an acyanotic infant is a ventricular septal defect, and a VSD murmur is generated by flow across a pressure gradient. At birth there is no gradient: pulmonary vascular resistance is still near systemic, so almost nothing crosses the defect and the newborn exam is normal.

Over the following weeks pulmonary vascular resistance falls, the gradient opens, shunt flow rises, and the murmur appears at 2 to 4 weeks. The same falling resistance explains the tachypnea and poor feeding, because increasing left-to-right shunt means pulmonary overcirculation. The normal two-week visit brackets the onset precisely, and the ductus was already closed by then.

edits.find: Which drug you want depends entirely on whether the ductus is the patient's lifeline or their problem. Ductal-dependent lesions — coarctation, pulmonary atresia, transposition, hypoplastic left heart — decompensate when it closes, so you reopen it. A preterm PDA shunting into the lungs is the problem, so you close it. And a softening murmur in an unrepaired large shunt is a warning, not an improvement.
edits.with: The drug choice depends entirely on whether the patient needs the ductus open or is harmed by it. Ductal-dependent lesions (coarctation, pulmonary atresia, transposition, hypoplastic left heart) decompensate when the ductus closes, so reopen it. A preterm PDA (patent ductus arteriosus) shunting into the lungs is the problem, so close it. A softening murmur in an unrepaired large shunt is a warning, not an improvement.
edits.note: danger: remove metaphor and em dashes, expand PDA
